messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated scaling quantification check - Aurora Labs late-stage

Folks —

Aurora is in final commercial review (see HubSpot link below) and Procurement is asking for a short validation we can deliver the dedicated capacity they need for Q3 ramp. They signed the SOW in principle but want an operational assurance that our node pool can support a 24/7 dedicated capacity of ~30 simultaneous A100-equivalent slots starting 2027-08-01.

Key asks:
- Quick inventory snapshot of current committed vs. free A100-equivalent slots by region (US-west preferred).
- Any known scheduled maint windows or migrations in July/Aug that would affect sustained throughput.
- Preliminary suggestion: hold (soft) 35 slots for AUR-2027-0524-01 until we finalize the MOU (7-day soft hold).

I attached a CSV export showing requested slot profile from the AE and a draft MOU from legal (aurora_mou_v1.pdf). Can we get a status by EOD tomorrow? If we can't offer a soft hold, call that out and propose acceptable alternatives (stagger, mixed-quantization, burst pool).

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
r.mendes@redwood.com

Attachments: gpu_inventory_snapshot.csv (CSV, 34 rows), aurora_mou_v1.pdf (PDF, 6 pages)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated scaling quantification check - Aurora Labs late-stage

On Mon, May 24, 2027 at 5:02 PM Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com> wrote:
> Folks —
>
> Aurora is in final commercial review ...

Rafael —

Quick inventory and ops readout below (pulled from provisioning DB and upcoming maintenance calendar):

Summary (US-west pool, production dedicated cluster):
- Total A100-equivalent slots (logical): 420
- Currently committed to other customers (reserved & committed): 368
- Free / unallocated (soft-available): 52
- Long-lead provisioning capacity (can create new logical slots via pooled overprovisioning and quantized packing): +16 over 3 weeks with standard lead (requires deployment shift, not hot add)

Notes and caveats:
- July maintenance window (control-plane upgrade) across 2 racks: 2027-07-10 -> 2027-07-12 (estimated 6–10% transient throughput drop for affected racks). Not an outage but may reduce sustained per-slot perf for the period.
- We have two large commits scheduled for late July from existing multi-year customers (they may convert warm standby to active). Their exact start dates are TBD but could consume 20–28 slots if they move forward on schedule.
- Engineering can accelerate a hot-add path (container + image warm cache) to create an extra ~12–16 A100-equivalent slots in ~10 business days, but that requires approvals for overtime and a brief maintenance window to warm images.

Operational recommendation:
1) Offer a 7-day soft hold for 35 slots (hold consumes soft-available pool) — this is feasible today but would reduce buffer to ~17 slots.
2) Concurrently schedule an expedited hot-add to increase capacity by ~12 slots (target complete by 2027-06-07) — requires ops signoff and a nominal CAPEX/crew OT estimate (Icc: $7.5k).
3) Add a fallback in the MOU: allow temporary burst routing to dedicated-compatible GPU variants (slightly higher variance on latency) for the first 30 days if scheduled commits materialize.

I can send the raw CSV inventory and a quick Ops readiness note to Legal/Finance for the MOU. Ben/Karthik — flag anything I missed from a commercial/commit perspective.

Neha Kapoor
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachment referenced: gpu_inventory_snapshot.csv

From: Amanda Lee <amanda@auroralabs.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Labs Procurement <procurement@auroralabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated scaling quantification check - Aurora Labs late-stage

Thanks Rafael & Neha —

Appreciate the quick readout. The soft hold for 35 slots sounds like a workable short-term step while we finalize commercial terms. Procurement endorses a 7-day soft hold. Two quick clarifications:

1) If the July maintenance causes a transient perf hit, can you commit to a performance SLA credit or at least a mitigation play (e.g., automatic routing to unaffected racks)?
2) If another customer converts and consumes the buffer, will we be notified prior to activation? We need an explicit escalation path.

We're prepared to sign the MOU once the operational hold is confirmed. I can route a DocuSign to Rafael once you confirm the soft hold.

— Amanda
Head of Platform Ops, Aurora Labs
amanda@auroralabs.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda@auroralabs.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated scaling quantification check - Aurora Labs late-stage

Amanda —

We will put a 7-day soft hold on 35 A100-equivalent slots in the US-west dedicated pool, effective immediately. Neha has noted the buffer impact and the July maintenance window; operations will provide an explicit mitigation plan (automatic routing and per-rack isolation) and a proposed credit language for the MOU (to cover transient perf delta).

Neha/Ben/Karthik — next steps:
- Neha: send Ops readiness note + CAPEX estimate for expedited hot-add by EOD Friday (2027-05-28).
- Ben: confirm commercial language tolerances for temporary burst routing and SLA credit mechanics.
- Karthik: update HubSpot deal stage to "Post-Contract Review" and attach the MOU Draft link.

Amanda, please send the DocuSign link when ready and I'll countersign the MOU. Thanks everyone — this moves us to legal/finance to close.

Rafael Mendes
